knowledge_answers.rationale: Once the toss winner's choice to bat or field is notified, it cannot be changed.
A batter may make ground with bat or person; grounding the bat behind the popping crease, without grounding beyond, places the batter within that ground.
The first fielding-side time-wasting instance creates a first and final warning; a further offence brings five Penalty runs to the batting side and reporting procedures.
The No-ball call contributes its one-run penalty; the struck boundary contributes four runs; struck runs are credited to the striker while the automatic run is a No-ball extra.

The delivery may be a Wide and still support Stumped; the keeper retained recognised status by remaining behind the wicket until the permitted point; out of ground, no attempted run and a fair keeper-only putting down complete Stumped, while the Wide penalty stands.
